newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister calls Algerian to calm row.
newsitem.headline: French minister calls Algerian to calm row.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette telephoned his Algerian counterpart Ahmed Attaf on Sunday to try to defuse a dispute over whether Paris was interfering in the North African country.

De Charette assured Attaf that French policy of non-interference in Algeria, racked by a civil war, had not changed, a French ministry statement said. Attaf asked France on Friday not to meddle in Algeria's internal affairs.

De Charette "expressed his solidarity with the Algerian people, victims of violence. He confirmed that French policy guidelines towards Algeria were unchanged from those he had expressed in the past," the statement said.

De Charette also said he would adopt the principles that Attaf wanted in Franco-Algerian relations -- "mutual respect based on non-interference, a balance of interests and coordination on matters of mutual interest".
An estimated 60,000 people have been killed since Algeria plunged into civil strife after the military authorities cancelled 1992 elections that Moslem fundamentalists were poised to win.

Attaf told France on Friday to stay out of Algeria's internal affairs after days of debate in France and calls by opposition Socialist leader Lionel Jospin and former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing for Paris to do more about the crisis.
